children: A git pull on prod fires the post-merge hook, which nukes the build, recompiles, and restarts Barkpark.

Deploying to Production is a git pull inside /opt/barkpark. The pull triggers .githooks/post-merge, which runs the canonical sequence: clean _build/prod completely, recompile, then restart the systemd Service. The wrappers make rebuild (nuke + recompile + restart) and make deploy (pull + the same) encode this so nobody has to remember the steps.

The full clean is non-negotiable. A partial clean — wiping only lib/barkpark — leaves stale HEEx templates from the Layouts module and prod serves old HTML for hours. ASDF must be on PATH for the recompile to find Elixir/Erlang, which is why the systemd Service's start.sh sources ASDF on boot. Expect a
while the BEAM comes back up.

Schema changes ship separately via Migration (mix ecto.migrate), not the post-merge hook. A code change that touches the Indx Engine index shape may need a Blue Green Rebuild afterward to repopulate bp_<scope>_vN. The Caddy front door keeps serving cached TLS while the app restarts, so external callers see only a brief gap.

Always smoke-test after: hit the HTTP API v1 (/api/schemas, /v1/data/query/...) and confirm LiveView Studio renders. A green deploy must still honour the Fresh Install Invariant — core Content Model up with all Plugins off.
